declared_in: reports/decision.md, section "Round 6: can the forecast beat the best simple rule? Area inputs, tested on 693 western counties never used (declared Nov 15, 2026, before any of those counties was loaded or scored)"
git_dirty_source_means: a file under src/ or a Python file in app/ differed from git_commit
what: Model E (the three-month outlook with area inputs) scored once on western counties never used before. Cost = 3 x missed + false alarms; lower is better, so a difference below zero favours the first-named.

model.forest: 300 trees, depth 14, min leaf 10, sqrt inputs, seed 0
model.trained_on: all 738 used counties, forward chaining 2008 to 2025

primary.name: 3-month cost: model E minus 'D2 or worse now'
primary.rows_used: all blind western counties: monthly issue rows, test years, full 52-week future known
primary.year_unit: the calendar year of the issue date (the date the forecast was made), all counties together

block1.caveat: Percentile interval from 18 resampled years (block 1). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.
